notes.text: Performance data is based on testing in accordance with ASHRAE Standard 70-2023, Method of Testing for Rating the Performance of Air Outlets and Inlets.

Sound levels are listed as NC and are based on a room absorption of 10 dB re 10-12 watts with a single grille. Adjust listed values for actual room absorption and the number of grilles serving the space.
NC values listed as "<15" indicate a sound level below NC 15.

All pressures are listed in inches water gauge (in. w.g.). Total pressure equals static pressure plus velocity pressure. Return grille pressures are listed as negative static pressure at the scheduled airflow.

Sizes are listed as nominal duct width x height in inches. Multiple nominal sizes share the same core area and are published with identical performance; flow rate equals core velocity times core area.

Border and frame style shall suit the mounting surface (surface, lay-in, exposed duct, or panel mount) indicated on the drawings. Contractor shall verify wall and ceiling construction, module size, and opening dimensions prior to release for fabrication.

Finish shall be the manufacturer's standard powder coat finish unless otherwise noted. Optional colors, custom colors, and anodized finishes on aluminum models are available; confirm lead time with the manufacturer.
Grille sizes and airflows shown are for bidding purposes. Contractor shall coordinate final selections with approved ductwork and equipment submittals.

A small number of misprints in the source catalogs have been corrected in this schedule: flow-rate cells inconsistent with the published core area x velocity identity (including the 0.46 sq ft row of the 93 and 99 tables), one LBMH throw value that disagrees with the identical LBP table, and a nominal size printed twice in the 99 and ATGH tables (listed here as 48 x 18 and 14 x 12, matching the other models). Suspected typos that could not be proven, such as irregular throw or sound values, are retained as printed.

Throw is listed in feet to terminal velocities of 150 fpm (minimum), 100 fpm (middle), and 50 fpm (maximum), shown in the schedule as 150-100-50. Throw data is based on supply air and room air at isothermal conditions; adjust listed throw for the scheduled heating or cooling temperature differential.

Listed deflection settings refer to horizontal blade deflection; total pressure and throw are listed for each published deflection setting. Balance and set blades to the air pattern indicated on the drawings.

Provide each supply grille with an opposed blade damper unless served by a terminal unit or otherwise noted. Published supply performance is based on a grille with an opposed blade damper installed; apply the manufacturer's published correction factors where no damper is provided.

Model designations: x10 = single deflection supply, x20 = double deflection supply; 500 Series = steel, 600 Series = aluminum, 700 Series = stainless steel construction. Blades are individually adjustable and may be furnished parallel to the long or short dimension.

Published data is based on core style 520 with an opposed blade damper. Corrections (total pressure multiplier / NC add): 510/610/710 with damper 1 / -4 at 0 deg, 1 / -1 at 22.5 deg, 1 / +4 at 45 deg; 520/620/720 without damper 0.85 / -7, 0.92 / -3, 0.93 / +3; 510/610/710 without damper 0.77 / -10, 0.80 / -6, 0.82 / +1.
For a 20 degree upward deflection, use the 0 degree throw rating with the 22.5 degree total pressure.

Steel borders feature reinforced, precision mitered corners and roll formed blades. Hospital grade construction with removable core and stainless steel 1/4 turn quick release fasteners is available on the 700 Series only. Minimum size 6 in. x 4 in.; maximum one-piece size 48 in. x 48 in.; oversized construction available with mullions and/or duct channels.

Options: fire rated construction (FR), insect screen (IS), light shield (LS), square to round adaptor (SR), return air silencer (RAS), and stainless steel opposed blade damper mounted to the back of the grille.

Louvered return grilles match and complement the louvered supply grilles. x10Z models have 0 degree fixed blades at 3/4 in. spacing; x30 models have 45 degree fixed blades at 3/4 in. spacing for minimal see-through; x35 models have 45 degree fixed blades at 1/2 in. spacing. 500 Series = steel, 600 = aluminum, 700 = stainless steel.
Published data is for a grille with an opposed blade damper in the full open position. Corrections with no damper: multiply pressure loss by 0.82 and subtract 12 from the listed NC.

Published data is for a grille with an opposed blade damper in the full open position. Corrections with no damper: multiply pressure loss by 0.91 and subtract 5 from the listed NC. Published data does not include the filter pressure drop on FF models or the effect of a ceiling radiation damper on fire rated models.

Published data is for a grille with an opposed blade damper in the full open position. Corrections with no damper: multiply pressure loss by 0.81 and subtract 2 from the listed NC. Published data does not include the filter pressure drop on FF models or the effect of a ceiling radiation damper on fire rated models.

Filter frame models (FF) accept standard 1 in. or 2 in. filter media with a removable hinge mechanism allowing hinged access or complete grille removal; 1/4 turn quick release or knurled screw latches, also available hingeless with latches on both sides. Hospital grade removable core construction (H) is available on the 700 Series.

Model 910 = single deflection, model 920 = double deflection (adds adjustable rear blades at 3/4 in. spacing). Front blades are individually adjustable at 1/2 in. spacing. Heavy gauge steel construction with smooth blades and countersunk screw holes, intended for gymnasiums, public restrooms, and heavy traffic corridors.

Published data is based on core style 520 with an opposed blade damper. Corrections without damper: multiply total pressure by 0.80 and adjust NC by -4 at 0 deg, -2 at 22.5 deg, +1 at 45 deg. With damper, add to NC: 0 at 0 deg, +2 at 22.5 deg, +6 (920) or +9 (910) at 45 deg.
For a 20 degree upward deflection, use the 0 degree throw rating with the 22.5 degree total pressure.

Minimum size 6 in. x 4 in.; maximum one-piece size 48 in. x 48 in.; oversized multi-section construction available. Options: mounting frame, steel opposed blade damper (VCS3), and 0 degree or 45 degree blade lock.

Linear bar grille performance is published per foot of active length: the scheduled flow rate is cfm per foot at the scheduled static pressure, and the row identity is the core (duct) height. Multiply cfm/ft by the active length in feet for total airflow.
NC values are based on a 10 ft active section. NC corrections for other active lengths (add): 1 ft -10, 2 ft -7, 4 ft -4, 6 ft -2, 8 ft -1, 10 ft 0, 15 ft +2, 20 ft +3, 25 ft +4, 30 ft +5.

Throw values are based on a 4 ft active section with a 20 degree F cooling differential, listed separately for sill-or-floor and sidewall mounting. Throw multipliers for other lengths: 1 ft active x0.5 / x0.6 / x0.7 and 10 ft or continuous x1.6 / x1.4 / x1.2 (at 150 / 100 / 50 fpm respectively).
For return air applications, add 4 to the listed NC and take negative static pressure as 0.8 times the listed static pressure.

Core style key - deflection: 0 deg = 15A/15B/25B/25C; 15 deg = 16A/16B/26B/26C; 30 deg = 27B/27C. Bar spacing: 1/4 in. (15A/16A), 1/2 in. (15B/16B/25B/26B/27B), 7/16 in. (25C/26C/27C). Provide the core style scheduled. Bar width depends on the core type: pressed core (LBP/LBPH) 3/32 in. (15A/15B), 1/8 in. (16A/16B), 3/16 in. (25B through 27C); heavy duty mandrel tube (LBMH) 1/8 in. (15A through 16B), 7/32 in. (25B through 27C).

1/2 in. spacing core styles (15B, 16B, 25B, 26B, 27B) are not for use in floor applications. Construction is extruded aluminum throughout; heavy duty models have removable cores held by core clips for access to dampers and equipment.

Frame styles: flanged borders 250/500/750/1000/1250, spring clip frames B and D for sill applications, concealed plaster frame (CPF, LBPH only), and narrow frames 125 and 187 for architectural flooring. Flanged borders include alignment plates for multi-section continuous runs; mitered corner sections available in flat, inside, and outside configurations.
Optional accessories: blank-off sections for a continuous appearance without airflow, directional vanes to shorten throw and increase spread, and volume dampers.
LBP = pressed core; LBPH = heavy duty pressed core suitable for light foot traffic floor applications.
LBMH = heavy duty mandrel tube core suitable for most floor applications. Curved (concave/convex) construction is exclusive to the LBM model in core styles 15A, 15B, and 25C only.

Egg crate return grille core styles: 80 = 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 in. grid; 81 = 1/2 x 1/2 x 1 in. grid; 82 = 1 x 1 x 1 in. grid (all 0 degree cores sharing one performance table); 85 = 45 degree angled sight-resistant core. Aluminum grid core with durable powder coat finish; the 80 Series has the largest free area of any grille for high capacity, low sound return and exhaust.
Grille tested without damper. Corrections for a grille with an opposed blade damper (VCS3/VCS3AL): multiply negative static pressure by 1.3 and add 6 to the listed NC.

Published data is based on an F border. For an ED border apply corrections for the reduced core area: listed core area 0.15-0.30 sq ft multiply total pressure by 2.4 and add 15 NC; 0.34-0.90: x1.9 +10; 1.07-1.80: x1.4 +5; 2.08-6.25: x1.2 +2.

Options: integrated plenum with top or side round inlet (80SR), filter frame (80FF/80FH) accepting 1 in. or 2 in. media, fire rated construction (FR), and mounting frame. Published data does not include filter pressure drop on filter frame models or the effect of a ceiling radiation damper on fire rated models.

Fire rated option is a UL listed assembly meeting NFPA 90A, incorporating a thermal blanket and butterfly type fire damper with a 165 F or 212 F fusible link; available for exposed grid (T-bar lay-in) ceilings only.
The 45 degree angled core obstructs the line of sight through the grille without requiring a light shield or plenum.

Perforated return grille with a 51 percent free area perforated core, designed to match perforated supply diffusers in appearance. Core material variants: 10 = steel, 10A = aluminum, 10SS = stainless steel.

Minimum size 6 in. x 4 in.; maximum single piece 24 in. x 48 in.; oversized multi-piece construction available. Options: mounting frame, steel or aluminum opposed blade damper, filter frame (10FF) accepting 1 in. or 2 in. media, and fire rated construction (10-FR, 10FF-FR).

Fire rated option is a UL listed assembly meeting NFPA 90A with a thermal blanket and curtain style fire damper (165 F or 212 F fusible link); available for exposed grid (T-bar lay-in) ceilings only. Published data does not include the ceiling radiation damper or filter pressure drop.

Heavy duty return gym grille lineup: 90 = steel 3/8 in. spacing 0 deg; 91 = steel 3/8 in. 45 deg; 93 = steel 1/2 in. 45 deg; 95 = steel 3/4 in. 0 deg; 96 = steel 3/4 in. 45 deg; 97 = extruded aluminum 1/2 in. 0 deg; 98 = extruded aluminum 1/2 in. 45 deg; 99 = extruded aluminum 1/2 in. 30 deg. FH suffix = filter frame variant sharing the base model's performance.

Fully welded heavy duty border construction with mandrel tubes supporting the blades, intended for gymnasiums, factories, warehouses, and heavy traffic public areas. Maximum one-piece size 48 in. x 96 in. in aluminum, 48 in. x 48 in. in steel.

Published data is rated with an opposed blade damper installed. Corrections without damper (negative static pressure multiplier / NC add): 90 x0.83 -4; 91 x0.93 -2; 93 x0.93 -2; 95 x0.87 -4; 96 x0.90 -5; 97 x0.87 -7; 98 x0.96 -2; 99 x0.87 -7.

Options: mounting frame; steel (VCS3), heavy duty steel (VCS5), or aluminum (VCS3AL) opposed blade damper; filter frame (FH models) accepting standard 1 in. or 2 in. filter media with quick release or piano hinge access; anodized finishes on aluminum models.
Model 98 is not recommended for core velocities in excess of 450 fpm.

Transfer grilles are designed for use in doors and partitions to allow transfer of air between spaces. STG = heavy duty steel; ATG1/ATG2 = aluminum; ATGH = heavy duty extruded aluminum with mandrel tube construction for industrial and severe use applications. Sight-proof models (STG, ATG1, ATGH) use finely spaced chevron blades; the light-proof ATG2 uses a double chevron blade finished in flat black to prevent light transfer.
Provide matching grilles on both faces of the door or partition where indicated. ATG1 sight-proof grilles are compatible with doors and partitions as thin as 1-3/8 in.
Negative static pressure for the light-proof ATG2 is two times the scheduled ATG1 value at the same airflow.
Maximum one-piece sizes: 32 in. x 36 in. aluminum (ATG1/ATG2), 48 in. x 30 in. heavy duty aluminum (ATGH), 48 in. x 36 in. steel (STG).
